summary: Initial discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Symmetry Health to understand security, compliance, and hosting constraints for an inference deployment. Main themes: must meet SOC 2/ISO baseline, prefer customer-managed KMS, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC scoping, audit log retention for 2 years, data residency in US-East. Symmetry leaning toward Dedicated for performance/isolation but wants private (VPC) option for certain PHI workloads. Next steps: share certs, network checklist, schedule pilot kick-off.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Michelle Alvarez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Lin (Head of Infra, Symmetry), Priya Rao (Security Engineer, Symmetry), Marta Kovac (Compliance Manager, Symmetry)

--- Auto-summary (brief) ---
Redwood: quick intro of hosted vs dedicated vs private; Symmetry: constraints about PHI, retention, KMS, SSO. Agreed to exchange documentation and plan pilot.

--- Topics ---
1) Compliance baseline (SOC2/ISO)
2) Authentication & SSO (SAML/Okta)
3) Encryption & KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)
4) RBAC / audit logs / retention
5) Hosting choices: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
6) Timeline and pilot scope

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00:03] Michelle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Michelle, account exec on the Redwood side, joining with Ravi who's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:11] Jared: Good thanks, Jared here. We have about an hour. We'll mostly focus on security and hosting constraints.
[00:00:18] Priya: Hi, Priya - security. Quick heads up, most of our questions are around KMS and retention for PHI, so we might dive deep.
[00:00:25] Marta: Marta as well, compliance will chime in on SOC2/ISO and audit windows.
[00:00:30] Ravi: Great. Real quick agenda: certs and compliance first, then auth, then encryption/kms, then logs/retention, then hosting options and a possible pilot plan. Does that work?
[00:00:39] Jared: Works.

[00:01:05] Michelle: Just to set context, Redwood offers hosted inference (our API), Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and a Private VPC option where you run inference in your VPC with a customer-controlled control plane. Many customers with health data use Dedicated or Private for PHI.
[00:01:22] Priya: When you say private VPC, is that full customer-managed networking? Like we put the inference instances in our subnet and we control egress?
[00:01:31] Ravi: Yes, the private deployment is deployed into your VPC. Redwood ships an appliance/controller that we manage the control plane for if you choose, or we can give you a self-managed on-prem bundle. Egress rules are yours; we recommend specific egress for metrics and control plane reachability.
[00:01:44] Jared: Ok. We need strong isolation for PHI — encryption at rest AND in transit with our keys. We can't hand keys to a vendor.
[00:01:52] Michelle: Understood. So customer-managed KMS is supported. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and we also have an HSM option for private deployments.
[00:02:03] Marta: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001? Can you share certs?
[00:02:09] Michelle: Yes we do SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 — I'll send the certs and the latest pen test summary after the call.
[00:02:15] Priya: Great. Also, audit logs: we need immutable, tamper-evident logs and retention for two years for certain workflows. What does Redwood offer?
[00:02:26] Ravi: We emit audit events for API access, model loads, role changes, and admin activity. For hosted customers we retain logs for X days by default, but for enterprise we can configure longer retention and ship logs to your S3 or SIEM. For Private, logs can remain in your environment entirely.
[00:02:40] Jared: When you say X days, can you give ballpark?
[00:02:44] Ravi: Default hosted retention is 90 days. For Dedicated or enterprise add-on, we commonly do 365 or more; since you mentioned two years, we can do 730-day retention by exporting to your S3 with object lock for immutability.

[00:03:12] Priya: Is the export push or can we pull? We want to control the retention lifecycle.
[00:03:18] Ravi: We can push logs to your S3 bucket using a customer-provided role; alternatively, you can pull via our event API if you prefer. For immutability we'd recommend S3 Object Lock with governance mode and a lifecycle policy.

[00:04:05] Marta: Ok that sounds promising. On encryption: full disk encryption on instances plus envelope encryption with our KMS?
[00:04:12] Ravi: Yes. Disk-level encryption plus application-layer encryption. For sensitive cache or KV cache — apologies we tend to say KV cache — we can encrypt the KV cache entries using your KMS CMKs. In private deployments the key never leaves your control.
[00:04:25] Priya: How about the model artifacts and versions — are those stored encrypted and do you allow us to control keys for model weights?
[00:04:31] Michelle: We can ensure model artifacts at rest are encrypted with your CMK for private deployments. For hosted/shrink-wrapped models we use Redwood-managed keys by default, but we do offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for Enterprise hosted customers for certain cases. There might be some operational constraints; Ravi can follow up.

[00:05:00] Ravi: Quick note on BYOK for hosted: technically we wrap model weight storage with your CMK, but runtime caching on shared infra can sometimes use ephemeral keys — that's why many regulated customers choose Dedicated or Private to avoid shared execution.
[00:05:15] Jared: Makes sense. Performance needs are also a factor. We have latency P95 SLO ~200ms for inference peaks; can Dedicated hit that with batching turned off?
[00:05:26] Ravi: With Dedicated and right instance type (4xA100 or similar) we can meet 200ms P95 for typical conversational models at moderate concurrency. Batching can increase throughput but at cost of latency, so we tune continuous batching parameters. For strict P95 low-latency, Private or Dedicated single-tenant is recommended.

[00:06:02] Priya: Authentication — we use Okta and SAML for SSO, SCIM for provisioning. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP and enforce RBAC?
[00:06:10] Michelle: Yes. SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported. We map IdP groups to Redwood roles so you can control admin vs developer access.
[00:06:18] Ravi: To add, we support SCIM v2 for group/user sync. For session duration and session revocation we support SAML single logout and can revoke tokens from the admin console or via API.
[00:06:29] Marta: We need separation of duties: only certain users can push model versions or change rollout policies. How granular is RBAC?
[00:06:36] Ravi: Roles are fairly granular: org admin, team admin, deployer, viewer, billing. We also have a policy engine for per-route permissions if you want to restrict who can call certain models. For private, you can also wire in your own IAM for even tighter controls.

[00:07:12] Jared: About data in flight — TLS 1.2 minimum? We have a requirement for TLS 1.2+ and prefer TLS 1.3 where possible.
[00:07:18] Ravi: We use TLS 1.3 in public endpoints; for internal control-plane traffic we use mTLS.

[00:07:30] Priya: Retention — beyond logs, what about request/response retention for generation outputs? We do want to ensure PHI isn't stored unless necessary.
[00:07:39] Michelle: By default, Redwood hosts short-term request retention to support debugging and quality monitoring. For PHI we recommend either disabling request retention, enabling on-prem/private where you control storage, or configuring automatic deletion after a short window. We can also mask or redact PII at ingestion if you supply rules.
[00:07:56] Priya: Can we disable user-level examples collection globally?
[00:08:00] Ravi: Yes, that's a flag on your org settings. For Dedicated/Private we typically turn off collection unless explicitly enabled.

[00:08:30] Marta: Audit scope: we need attestations about who accessed what model and who changed a rollout — is that all in the audit trail?
[00:08:38] Ravi: Yes, audit trail includes user id, action, resource, timestamp, IP (if applicable), and request-id. For higher assurance we can sign log exports and time-stamp them.

[00:09:05] Jared: Any pen testing we should be aware of? Do customers run their own pen tests on private deployments?
[00:09:11] Michelle: We run an annual third-party pentest and will share the summary. Customers can run their own tests on Dedicated or Private; for hosted we have a coordinated process. We require a test window and scoping conversation so we don't impact shared infra.

[00:09:45] Priya: How about data residency? We're required for some studies to keep data in US-East only. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[00:09:53] Ravi: Yes — we support region pinning for model serving. For hosted, we have region options; for Dedicated and Private you control region via the deployment. We can also pin control plane metadata to particular regions for compliance; there are some tradeoffs we can document.

[00:10:22] Michelle: Quick commercial note — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation; Private is more like bringing a Redwood runtime into your network. Many regulated health customers start with Dedicated then migrate sensitive workloads to Private.
[00:10:36] Jared: Timeline — we're targeting a pilot to validate latency and key integrations in ~3 weeks. Is that realistic?
[00:10:43] Ravi: Yes. If we get access to a test VPC and your KMS role, we can spin a Dedicated pilot environment in about 2 weeks, maybe less. Private might take longer for network setup, but doable in 3-4 weeks depending on approvals.

[00:11:15] Priya: On the KMS integration detail — do you require a grant model or do we provide a key that Redwood services can call? We can't give full kms:Decrypt to external accounts ordinarily.
[00:11:25] Ravi: For AWS KMS, the recommended pattern is to create a key policy granting the Redwood cross-account IAM role only decrypt/encrypt for the necessary resource ARNs (artifact buckets, cache encryption). We also support using KMS grants for temporary access. For Private, the key stays in your account and the runtime uses a role within your VPC.
[00:11:43] Priya: That addresses our chief concern. We'll want an explicit example policy.
[00:11:49] Michelle: I'll include a sample key policy and the minimal IAM role for the S3/log export and KMS usage.

[00:12:20] Marta: Regarding SOC2 evidence — we may ask for your control matrices mapped to our control set. Do you have a shared control mapping doc?
[00:12:29] Michelle: We have an SOC2 control map and a compliance pack for prospects. I'll attach that with the certs.

[00:13:10] Jared: One more thing — do you have support for on-prem hardware GPUs if we wanted to keep everything air-gapped for certain models?
[00:13:18] Ravi: Yes, we offer an on-prem package. It's our least common path but viable for air-gapped requirements. It includes the runtime, a control plane that can be fully customer-managed, and an HSM integration path.

[00:13:50] Priya: For monitoring and alerts, can we integrate with our PagerDuty and our SIEM?
[00:13:56] Ravi: Yes. We support alert webhooks to PagerDuty, and log exports to SIEM via S3 or direct syslog/forwarder depending on your stack.

[00:14:25] Michelle: Any blockers we haven't covered?
[00:14:29] Jared: So far the main blockers are keys and retention. We'll need to confirm legal sign-off on data processing terms for PHI.
[00:14:36] Marta: Also, our compliance team will need the pen test report and SOC2/ISO mapping.

[00:14:50] Priya: A small gotcha: we have strict egress control so outbound requests must be to a whitelist. How does your control plane communicate? Can you document the IPs/dns?
[00:14:59] Ravi: Yes, we provide a published connectivity list — ranges and FQDNs for the control plane and registry. For private we only need a few endpoints and you can restrict them. We'll provide those in the VPC checklist.

[00:15:34] Jared: Cost question briefly — if we export logs to S3 for long-term retention, is that part of Redwood billing, or will we be billed directly by cloud provider?
[00:15:41] Michelle: Exported storage costs are billed by your cloud provider. Redwood can include the cost to ship and process logs in the managed service pricing if you want us to handle lifecycle, otherwise we can hand off.

[00:16:05] Priya: For the pilot, what minimum information do you need from us to get started?
[00:16:11] Ravi: A test VPC CIDR, subnet IDs for the nodes, an S3 bucket for logs (or we can provide one), and a KMS CMK ARN with a role or policy that allows Redwood's provisioning role limited decrypt. Also a contact for network setup and a list of models you'd like to test.
[00:16:36] Michelle: We'll follow up with a checklist.

[00:17:05] Jared: On the model side, we have two workloads: general triage chat (non-PHI) and a structured summary generator that occasionally touches PHI. The latter will need to be in Private or Dedicated with BYOK and two-year logs.
[00:17:20] Priya: Exactly. Non-PHI can be hosted, but we want the sensitive pipeline fully isolated.

[00:17:55] Ravi: Implementation approach we suggest: spin up a Dedicated environment for the pilot for both workloads (isolated pool), integrate KMS for encryption, map SAML groups for RBAC, and export logs to your S3 with object lock for the PHI pipeline. If pilot goes well, migrate PHI to Private for air-gapped or on-prem if required.

[00:18:30] Marta: Do you support label-based routing so requests flagged as PHI route to Private/Dedicated automatically?
[00:18:38] Ravi: We have routing policies where you can route by route, model, or header. You can add a header or tag on requests and route them to the PHI-dedicated pool; that can be automated in your app.

[00:19:05] Priya: About revocation — if we need to rotate keys or revoke access to the runtime, how fast can that be enforced?
[00:19:11] Ravi: Key rotation is supported; for immediate revocation we recommend revoking the IAM role or changing key policy and we support emergency stop via the management API. In Private deployments, you own the keys so you can revoke instantly.

[00:19:45] Jared: Any data processed in model embeddings or vector stores — are those considered persisted?
[00:19:52] Michelle: Embeddings and vectors can be persisted in your datastore or in Redwood-managed vector stores. For PHI we strongly recommend you persist them in your own VPC-backed store, encrypted with your keys. We'll document our recommended patterns.

[00:20:28] Ravi: small point: sometimes we call the metadata store the 'embedding store' or 'vecstore' — apologies if the transcriptions called it something else earlier, \"K-V cash\" versus \"KV cache\".
[00:20:37] Priya: (laughs) yeah transcription got creative.

[00:21:05] Marta: On legal — we'll need DPA and a BAAs for PHI. Do you sign BAAs?
[00:21:12] Michelle: Redwood does sign BAAs for customers with PHI requirements; terms are part of our Enterprise agreement. Legal can share a template; I'll loop in our legal contact.

[00:21:42] Jared: Ok good. Any limitations on model updates/rollouts with canary testing under Dedicated or Private?
[00:21:50] Ravi: Canary and A/B rollouts are supported. We also have automatic fallback to a stable variant if latency or error rates spike. Those policies are configurable per-deployment.

[00:22:18] Priya: For the pilot success criteria, from our side: 1) P95 latency under 300ms for the PHI pipeline at test concurrency, 2) key integration working with no key material leaving our account, 3) logs exported and immutable, 4) RBAC and SAML provisioning complete.
[00:22:34] Michelle: That's great, we'll build an acceptance checklist that maps to those four items.

[00:23:00] Ravi: I'll also prepare a short runbook for the pilot that includes network steps, sample policies, and troubleshooting.

[00:23:30] Jared: Is there any reason we should not do Dedicated for the pilot? I want minimal friction.
[00:23:36] Michelle: Dedicated is often the fastest path for regulated customers because it gives isolation and avoids some of the BYOK caveats in hosted. Private takes more network coordination. For your timeline, Dedicated pilot is recommended.

[00:24:05] Priya: Ok let's do Dedicated. A couple more technical clarifications — do you persist KV cache between restarts? We need determinism for certain requests.
[00:24:14] Ravi: KV cache is modular: you can persist it to a customer-managed store if you want, or leave it ephemeral. Persisting is possible but there are tradeoffs for warm-up times. We'll document options.

[00:24:45] Marta: We'll also need to know about your patch cadence for runtime images and how you notify customers of security updates.
[00:24:52] Michelle: We publish a monthly security bulletin and notify on critical patches immediately. For Dedicated/Private we coordinate maintenance windows with customers.

[00:25:18] Priya: Any E2E encryption concerns for embeddings in vector DBs? We've seen a lot of vendors claim encryption but then keys are still held by them.
[00:25:26] Ravi: For RD-managed vector stores we use service-level encryption but keys may be managed by Redwood unless BYOK is enabled. For PHI we recommend your own vector DB in your VPC encrypted with your CMKs. We'll provide patterns for Pinecone-like services or S3-based stores.

[00:26:00] Jared: Sounds good. Let's talk quick about legal timeline. Marta, how long do you think compliance signoff will take after we get documents?
[00:26:08] Marta: If we get SOC2, pen test summary, and key policies this week, we can do initial review in 7-10 business days, but BAAs take additional cycles with legal. So maybe 2-3 weeks for full signoff depending on redlines.

[00:26:30] Michelle: We'll aim to get those docs in the next 48 hours.

[00:27:00] Priya: For the demo/pilot data — do you have a recommended scrubbing approach or mock dataset generator?
[00:27:08] Ravi: We have a small test harness and sanitized dataset templates we can share. Also can set up a masked proxy to strip PII before hitting the model endpoints.

[00:27:40] Jared: Excellent. Any other questions from your side?
[00:27:44] Priya: Can you send us a sample SAML assertion mapping for group roles so we can align Okta?
[00:27:51] Michelle: Yep, sample SAML mapping and SCIM group mapping will be included in the checklist.

[00:28:20] Marta: For the audit log schema, can you include an example of the JSON payload so we can map fields to our SIEM?
[00:28:27] Ravi: Absolutely — I'll include a sample payload and event IDs.

[00:28:50] Michelle: Recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2/ISO certs and pen test; Ravi will produce network & KMS example policies and an initial pilot runbook; Jared will provide VPC details and Priya will provide retention/classification info. We'll target pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-11.
[00:29:07] Jared: That works.

[00:29:25] Priya: One last nit: how do you handle debugging traces that might include full prompt text? That could expose PHI.
[00:29:33] Ravi: We redact prompt text in debug dumps for PHI-marked pipelines by default when the no-retention flag is set; otherwise debug traces are available only in the customer's S3 export. We'll note that in the runbook.

[00:30:05] Michelle: Great. We'll get those items out. Thanks everyone.
[00:30:09] Jared: Thanks.
[00:30:12] Priya: Thanks.
[00:30:15] Marta: Thanks.

--- End of captured transcript (some sections redacted for brevity).

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (\"K-V cash\" -> KV cache, \"SAM El\" -> SAML). Some cross talk. Action items and next steps recorded in metadata above.
